newsitem.title: NORWAY: FIBA looks into alleged irregularities.
newsitem.headline: FIBA looks into alleged irregularities.

text.p: Norwegian holding company FIBA ASA said on Friday its broker subsidiary FIBA Nordic Securities AS was probing if a London-based FIBA-linked broker could be criticised for the way it worked for Morgan Grenfell funds.

FIBA at the same time reiterated a denial from FIBA Nordic Securities (UK) Ltd that it was involved in alleged irregularities in the business of three investment funds under the Morgan Grenfell umbrella.
The London-based broker, also known as Fiba Nordic Securities (FNS), said on Thursday it welcomed investigation from any regulator.
"Listed company FIBA's wholly-owned subsidiary (broker firm) FIBA Nordic Securities AS holds a 10 percent stake in FIBA Nordic Securities (UK) Ltd, which was established in 1993," the statement said.

"As minority shareholder and cooperation partner FIBA Nordic Securities AS has taken steps in cooperation with the English company (FIBA Nordic Securities (UK) Ltd) to clarify if the English company, in carrying out tasks for the Morgan Grenfell funds, has behaved in a manner that could be subject to criticism."

FNS sold unlisted securites to, and valued securites for the three funds managed by Peter Young and Stewart Armer, who have both now been suspended by Morgan Grenfell Asset Management, part of the Deutsche Bank Group.
Press reports and fund management sources have suggested that the relationship between FNS and Young was unusually close.

"Norwegian and foreign newspapers have in the last few days carried articles linking London-based FIBA Nordic Securities (UK) Ltd to suspicions of irregularities in three investment funds administered by Morgan Grenfell," the FIBA statement said.

"Hints in the newspapers that Fiba Nordic Securities (UK) Ltd either directly or indirectly has contributed to irregularities surrounding the Morgan Grenfell funds are rejected by Fiba Nordic securities (UK) Ltd. The company's lawyers and auditors are investigating the matter," it said.
